builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Improving JEV Entailment Reranking with Span Readouts and Selective Adaptation
summary: The method replaces option-ending pointer readouts with mean pooling over the contextualized states inside each NLI option, and replaces full all-module adapter tuning with low-rank updates restricted to attention and gated DeltaNet projections, dropping feed-forward adapters. It adds no head parameters and reduces trainable parameters by more than half, lowering fine-tuning memory and compute while claiming higher reranking accuracy. It can fail because results are reported on a single 4B model and one aggregate benchmark (MC11), so gains may not transfer to other backbones, domains, or reranking workloads.
rationale: The approach is cheap to implement and fits constrained infrastructure, but evidence is limited to one model and one benchmark, so it warrants workload-specific validation before production adoption.
technique: Mean-span readout with selective adapter pruning for NLI reranking

claims.statement: The method replaces option-ending pointer readouts with mean pooling over the contextualized states inside each NLI option, and replaces full all-module adapter tuning with low-rank updates restricted to attention and gated DeltaNet projections, dropping feed-forward adapters. It adds no head parameters and reduces trainable parameters by more than half, lowering fine-tuning memory and compute while claiming higher reranking accuracy. It can fail because results are reported on a single 4B model and one aggregate benchmark (MC11), so gains may not transfer to other backbones, domains, or reranking workloads.

On MC11, selective adaptation improves NeoHorse-1-4B accuracy over the all-module baseline while cutting trainable parameters by more than half; mean-span pooling adds further consistent gains at the same parameter count.
